key_insight: NLP of routine EHR notes uncovered symptom-based motor neuron disease subtypes that were more informative than traditional onset-site labels.
clinical_relevance: These data-driven phenotypes could help clinicians better estimate prognosis and tailor supportive supportive care, especially for patients with respiratory or autonomic symptom burden.
method: MedCAT extracted symptom mentions from clinical notes and removed negated concepts.
Symptoms were filtered to UMLS sign/symptom terms and converted into binary patient profiles.
Latent class analysis grouped patients into symptom-based clusters, with survival compared using Kaplan-Meier, log-rank tests, and Cox models.
evidence_signal: In 2,361 confirmed MND patients, the study found significant survival differences across clusters (log-rank p < 0.001) in both first-note and all-notes analyses.
watch_item: The findings come from a single tertiary neurology center and rely on documentation quality, so external validation and careful handling of missing or inconsistent symptom recording are needed.
paper_title: Symptom-based phenotype discovery in motor neuron disease using natural language processing of electronic health records
